cues.text: Orphaned by twelve and turned away from job after job by a body too frail for ordinary labor, Alfred Bessette seemed an unlikely candidate.
He asked to join the Congregation of Holy Cross in Montreal, carrying only a note from his old pastor that read, 'I am sending you a saint.'
Assigned the lowly post of doorkeeper at a college for more than forty years, Brother André spent his days praying with the sick and desperate who came to him.
He attributed every healing that followed not to himself but to St. Joseph, to whom he had a lifelong devotion.
Out of nickel haircuts and small donations he raised, against every expectation, the funds to begin what would become Saint Joseph's Oratory, now one of the largest shrines in the world.
When he died in 1937, nearly a million mourners filed past his body in the depths of a Quebec winter, and in 2010 he became the first Canadian-born man to be declared a saint.
